title: Which numbers does every test divide?
description: Ten and eight together cover two, four, five, eight and ten. The video tests five numbers with the last digit and the last three digits, and finds the three that pass.
teaching_notes: One idea: two tests are enough, a zero at the end for ten and the last three digits for eight. Watch for students who test all five numbers one by one, or who say a number ending in zeros fails for eight.

video_script.why: The child cuts the five divisibility tests down to two, runs the last digit test first, and then runs the last three digits test on the numbers that are left.
video_script.substitution: Cut the five tests down to ten and eight, test the last digit for ten, then test the last three digits for eight.
video_script.anchor: five number cards in a row: 572, 2352, 5600, 6000 and 77622160, with a test strip of 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10 above them
video_script.payoff_line: Five thousand six hundred, six thousand and the last number pass both tests

final_answer.spoken: five thousand six hundred, six thousand, and seventy seven million six hundred and twenty two thousand one hundred and sixty

maths_rules: if 8 divides a number, then 4 and 2 divide it; if 10 divides it, then 5 and 2 divide it; so the tests 10 and 8 cover all five
10 divides a number when its last digit is 0
8 divides a number when its last three digits make a multiple of 8
572 and 2352 end in 2, so 10 does not divide them
5600 ends in 0 and 600 = 8 x 75; 6000 ends in 0 and 000 = 0 x 8
video_script.design: One idea: run the cheap test first and then the three digits test, because two tests cover all five numbers. Callback to the observation about the last three digits. Wrong idea: none is broken. The five cards stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; five number cards 572, 2352, 5600, 6000 and 77622160, with a strip of tests 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10 above them and a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about five numbers.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two numbers are five hundred and seventy two, and two thousand three hundred and fifty two.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next two are five thousand six hundred, and six thousand.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last is seventy seven million six hundred and twenty two thousand one hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of them are divisible by two, four, five, eight and ten, all at once?

beats.on_screen: the five cards hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the test for 10: the last digit is 0; the test for 8: the last three digits make a multiple of 8

marks.ten: the words last digit is zero are written under the card 10
marks.eight: the words last three digits are written under the card 8

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten divides a number when its last digit is zero.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight divides a number when its last three digits make a multiple of eight.

beats.on_screen: Given: the numbers 572, 2352, 5600, 6000, 77622160; the tests 2, 4, 5, 8 and 10

marks.given: the five numbers and the five tests are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five numbers, and five tests that must all pass.

beats.on_screen: To find: the numbers that every test divides

marks.find: the words the numbers that pass every test are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the numbers that pass every test.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, cut the tests down: 8 covers 4 and 2; 10 covers 5 and 2; so run only 10 and 8

marks.cut: the strip of five tests is cut down
marks.eight: an arrow goes from 8 to 4 and to 2
marks.ten: an arrow goes from 10 to 5 and to 2

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, cut the five tests down to two.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>If eight divides a number, so do four and two.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>If ten divides it, so do five and two.
<bookmark mark='left'/>That leaves two tests to run, which are ten and eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the last digit first: 572 and 2352 end in 2, so 10 does not divide them; both are out

marks.first: the last digit 2 of 572 is circled
marks.second: the last digit 2 of 2352 is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, test the last digit first. Five hundred and seventy two ends in two.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Two thousand three hundred and fifty two also ends in two.
<bookmark mark='out'/>Ten divides neither of them, so both are out.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, 5600 and 6000 end in 0; 600 = 8 x 75; 000 = 0 x 8; both pass

marks.zero: the last digit 0 of 5600 and of 6000 is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step three, look at the next two numbers. Both end in zero, so ten divides them.
<bookmark mark='six'/>The last three digits of five thousand six hundred are six hundred, which is eight times seventy five.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>The last three digits of six thousand are all zeros, which is zero eights.
<bookmark mark='pass'/>Both pass both tests.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, 77622160 ends in 0; 160 = 8 x 20; it passes

marks.end: the last digit 0 of 77622160 is circled
marks.hun: the last three digits 160 are circled and 160 = 8 x 20 is written
marks.pass: a tick appears on the card

narration: <bookmark mark='end'/>Step four, look at the last number. It ends in zero, so ten divides it.
<bookmark mark='hun'/>Its last three digits are one hundred and sixty, which is eight times twenty.
<bookmark mark='pass'/>It passes both tests.

marks.check: 5600 = 8 x 700 = 10 x 560 is written and a tick appears
marks.six: 6000 = 8 x 750 = 10 x 600 is written and a tick appears

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check by multiplying. Eight times seven hundred is five thousand six hundred.
Ten times five hundred and sixty is the same.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Eight times seven hundred and fifty is six thousand. Ten times six hundred is the same.
<bookmark mark='out'/>The first two numbers fail the test for ten.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Five thousand six hundred, six thousand and the last number pass both tests.
